thread:
pagerduty: Paging: p99 latency breach on hosted-text-generation from 20:02 UTC, multiple customers affected, auto-escalation to oncall. SLO p99 > 2.5s, currently ~5s, increased streaming stalls. Incident ticket: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026

Alice (oncall): I'm on it. Reproducing signal in dashboards now. p95 ~ 700ms, p99 ~ 5.1s, streaming success rate dropped to 86% on pool shared-gpu-3.

Ben (sre): Noted. Any noisy tenant flagged? I see a spike in NVMe writeback and cgroup IO throttles on hosts in pool shared-gpu-3. Kernel writeback bursts at same timestamps.

Carol (eng-runtime): Getting lots of KV cache eviction logs and streaming stall traces in the runtime: ``[kvcache] evicting prefix 0x7f... due to mem_pressure`` and ``stream: stall detected seq=1245 wait_ms=4200``. Might be correlated.

Alice (oncall): Timeline: around 19:58 UTC eviction rate jumps, 20:01 host-level iostat shows heavy write IOPS, then p99 jumps. Could be noisy neighbor doing heavy checkpointing.

Derek (evac-coord): If it's multi-tenant IO, we should start host evacuations for the worst-affected machines. Which hosts? Carol, can you list top 3 host IDs by p99 contribution?

Carol (eng-runtime): Top hosts: gpu-3-12, gpu-3-15, gpu-3-18. gpu-3-15 is 44% of p99s. ssh to host shows "dropped packets" and heavy /var/lib/models writeback.

Ben (sre): I'll check cgroups on gpu-3-15. Running: ``sudo systemd-cgls --controllers=io`` then ``cat /sys/fs/cgroup/io/docker/<cid>/io.stat``

ops-bot: Runbook step: if noisy-tenant IO > 40% of p99 and writeback high, trigger eviction + reassign traffic. See playbook: https://redwood.playbooks/noisy-tenant.

Alice (oncall): Starting graceful evacuation of tenant traffic from gpu-3-15. Derek, start reassign and pause new allocations to that host.

Derek (evac-coord): Kicking eviction job now. Command used: ``rw-evacuate-host --host gpu-3-15 --dry-run=false --reassign=true --max-inflight=20``. ETA ~ 90s per slot. I'll post updates.

Eve (customer-success): Heads up to CS: customers X and Y saw degraded responses, some streaming sessions timed out. I'll draft a proactive note to impacted accounts after we stabilize.

Carol (eng-runtime): Added temporary firewall to stop long-running checkpointing jobs from writing to local NVMe on that host while we drain: ``tc qdisc add dev nvme0 root tbf rate 400mbit burst 32k`` — observing drop in write latency immediately.

Ben (sre): cgroup io stats before/after drain: ``read_bytes: 1.2GiB write_bytes: 14.8GiB`` for offending container. After stopping, write_bytes rate fell 10x. Kernel shows blk_throttle_time spiking earlier.

Alice (oncall): p99 started trending down to ~3.2s now. Still above SLO but improving. Streaming stalls count decreased from 420 -> 120 in the last 5m.

Derek (evac-coord): Host gpu-3-15 drain finished for high-priority tenants. I've rebalanced traffic to gpu-3-22 and gpu-4-02. No service restarts required; connections gracefully drained.

Carol (eng-runtime): We also enabled fallback routing: requests with latency > 2s are being routed to a quantized model variant in a different pool (dedicated-quant) to keep tail low. Config snippet: ``routing.fallback.threshold_ms=2000``

Ben (sre): I'm keeping an eye on kernel writeback queues. Suggest we throttle disk io for non-critical tenants cluster-wide for next 30m to avoid recurrence. Is that acceptable?

Alice (oncall): Approve throttling for batch/long-run workloads. Derek, add policy to pause batch jobs on shared-gpu pools for 30m.

Derek (evac-coord): Done: ``batch-control pause --pools shared-gpu-3,shared-gpu-4 --duration 30m``. Ops dashboard shows batch backlog cleared.

Eve (customer-success): Notifying impacted customers now (templated note). Will provide update once p99 < 2.5s for 10m.

Carol (eng-runtime): Quick log snippet from runtime during peak: ```
[streamer] stall_detected tenant=tenant-42 req=0x9f3 wait_ms=5178 kv_evictions=23
[allocator] mem_pressure=1.0 reclaim=120MB
[kvcache] evict prefix=0x7f count=12
```

Ben (sre): After mitigation p95=630ms p99=1.9s for last 5m window on hosted-text-generation. Streaming success 98%. Recommend we keep monitoring for 20m and then close incident.

Alice (oncall): Agreed. I'll keep the incident open and transition to postmortem if clean. @Derek please document evacuation start/end timestamps in the ticket.

Derek (evac-coord): Logged in INC-2026: evacuation started 20:04:17 UTC, drain complete 20:08:42 UTC, traffic rebalanced. Also added note: throttled batch jobs 20:09 UTC.

Eve (customer-success): Sent update to impacted customers at 20:15 UTC. One asked for SLA credit guidance — I'll coordinate with Sales.

pagerduty: Reminder: If p99 breaches again within 60 minutes, escalate to oncall+platform lead automatically.

Alice (oncall): Will monitor. For the postmortem we should look at: tenant checkpointing safeguards, cgroup io limits, proactive batching throttle policies, and whether routing fallback was invoked correctly.

Carol (eng-runtime): I'll capture debug traces and upload to INC-2026 with KV eviction counts per tenant. Also will add a runtime metric for "kv_eviction_rate" to detect this earlier.

Ben (sre): Suggested long-term: enforce per-tenant IO guardrails (rate limit writes), and enrich alerts to tie p99 increases to host-level writeback metrics automatically.

Alice (oncall): Closing the live mitigation: system stable, p99 < SLO for 12m. We'll keep the incident open for postmortem items. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Eve (customer-success): Copy that. I'll follow up with customers tomorrow with summary and mitigation details.

Carol (eng-runtime): Filing a model-routing follow-up PR to make the fallback policy smarter around streaming sessions.```
